relevance_note: Case report of one boy with GFAP variant and Alexander disease: 'a GFAP pathogenic germline variant (c.716G>T p.(Arg239Leu))' and 'Neonatal Alexander disease.'; his mother was tested and found mosaic.
method_note: Single case report; built by a short Python script from my own reading, with all spans checked verbatim against the Markdown. Two in-scope people: the proband ('patient', rule 5; 'Our patient' is a role word) and his tested mother ('mother of patient'), who 'showed maternal somatic mosaicism for this variant'; she gets a variant row with zygosity 'mosaic' (germline status of her mosaicism not stated; paper calls it somatic mosaicism, not tumour tissue). Proband inheritance recorded as 'inherited maternal' because the paper states the mother carries the same variant (mosaic); the father is not mentioned as tested. Proband zygosity and variant type left not reported (not stated). Mother's variant pathogenicity left not reported (stated for the proband's variant only). Age at onset taken as 'from a few weeks of age' (developmental concern); first seizure at 2 months is recorded on the seizure feature. Age at diagnosis not given (genetic result 'available post-mortem'); age at death not given; cause of death not explicitly stated (status epilepticus, then withdrawal of ventilatory support), so left not reported. Checklist judgments: 'eye movement abnormality' observed from 'absent oculocephalic reflexes' and ictal left eye deviation; 'spasticity or pyramidal signs' left not reported (paper says 'generalised hypertonia' only); 'recurrent vomiting' left not reported (vomiting stated but not as recurrent); 'medulla or cervical spinal cord' left not reported (MRI 'no intramedullary lesions' vs autopsy 'brain stem was pale and atrophic' and medullary Rosenthal fibres - not a stated medullary atrophy/signal abnormality); basal ganglia/thalamus observed from autopsy white matter change in those regions. 'Asymptomatic' mother recorded as excluded 'symptoms' only; it excludes no specific checklist item. Normal findings recorded as excluded abnormality: 'spared pupillary responses' -> absent pupillary responses; 'could suck' -> inability to suck. No contradictions found in the paper. No tables, no supplementary material.

span: Craniotomy, brain biopsy and third ventriculostomy were performed.
Our patient was commenced on vincristine and carboplatin
culture‐positive febrile neutropenia treated with intravenous antibiotics
requiring a ventriculoperitoneal shunt. Subsequent EEGs demonstrated frequent sustained seizure activity from different hemispheric foci. Nasogastric feeding was commenced
requiring anticonvulsants, intubation and ventilation. Following extensive discussion with the team and the family, ventilatory support was withdrawn
